models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light NE'lies and a flat sea over the islands now - but the trip dates are still a week out and unforecastable.
briefing.synopsis: The current pattern over the Aeolians is a weak, slack gradient with winds backing between NE and N: ECMWF IFS 0.25° (26 Sep 00Z), ECMWF AIFS (26 Sep 06Z) and ICON-2i (26 Sep 00Z) agree on 6-10 kt at the exposed islands today, easing to 1-4 kt by the 28th. Seas are small throughout - MFWAM and ECMWF WAM (both 26 Sep 00Z) put total wave at 1.6-2.5 ft today, dropping to 0.5-0.9 ft by Monday. If a pattern like this held into the trip it would mean motor-sailing more than sailing, with anchorage choice driven by comfort rather than shelter. The model data only reaches 2 Oct 23:00, so the departure date of 3/4 Oct and everything after it is beyond the horizon - I have no forecast for the trip itself.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Tonight is Portorosa Marina, an enclosed basin with all-round shelter, so the berth choice does not matter in this pattern. Portorosa is showing 5.1 kt from the N with gusts to 12.4 kt at 18:00 and wave 1.4 ft (consensus, 26 Sep runs). Nothing in the payload would push the fleet to move.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Saturday 27 Sep looks similar and light: Portorosa 3.5 kt NNE at 06:00 easing through the day, Lipari 7.8 kt NNE at 06:00 - though the models spread 4.1-10.9 kt at that hour, so treat the mean with caution. Waves 1.5-2.3 ft across the group, smallest in the lee. Any morning departure window is wide open in this pattern; the constraint is boat speed, not weather.

passage_notes.note: Go at 3.3 kt on a run; gusts to 10 kt against a 3 kt mean, single-model interval max.

cautions: The forecast reaches only 2 Oct 23:00. Every trip date is beyond it; the rehearsal verdicts are the real legs scored against this week's weather, not forecasts for 4-8 Oct.
Stromboli's Marina del Gabbiano scores only 'workable' even in this calm - it is open from every direction, so shelter there depends entirely on the sea staying down. Worth flagging now for planning.
Where 'models_range_kt' appears (e.g. Lipari 27 Sep 06:00, 4.1-10.9 kt; Portorosa 28 Sep 00:00, 0.5-7.0 kt) the models differ by more than 6 kt - the mean is not a reliable number at those hours.
IFS gust figures are interval maxima, so the large gust factors in 2-4 kt air (e.g. 10.5 kt gust on 3.8 kt mean at Portorosa) overstate what you will feel.
briefing.confidence_note: Run-to-run stability is good at short range (mean wind shift 0.6 kt at 0-24 h, 1.0 kt with 60° of direction scatter at 72-120 h), but the trip dates sit entirely beyond the 2 Oct model horizon, so no confidence can be attached to them at all.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
